claim: Google commits new water-stressed facilities to air-cooled systems during normal operations, while Microsoft's zero-water cooling design aims to eliminate evaporative water entirely and claims 125 million liters saved per facility per year.
shortLabel: Zero-water cooling is becoming a real design path
displayValue: Up to 125M liters saved per facility each year
comparisonContext: The tradeoff remains real, but zero-water cooling is emerging as an engineering path rather than only a sacrifice story.
scopeNote: Google's air-cooling commitment is well supported; Microsoft's zero-water performance claims remain company-reported rather than independently benchmarked.
sourceTitle: Measuring the environmental impact of delivering AI at Google Scale
